2025-01-14 09:12:08 | Ticket ID: CT-541882 | Agent: Maya Chen
Customer contacted support via chat regarding intermittent Wi-Fi drops on a Contoso AuraBook 14. Customer stated the laptop would stay connected for 10 to 20 minutes, then lose internet access while still showing the home network as connected. Issue appeared most often after waking from sleep. Customer had already rebooted the router and confirmed other household devices remained online during the drops.

Chat transcript excerpt:
Customer: Hi, my AuraBook keeps dropping Wi-Fi after sleep. It says connected, but pages do not load.
Agent Maya Chen: I can help with that. Does toggling Wi-Fi off and back on restore service temporarily?
Customer: Yes, usually for a while. Then it happens again.
Agent Maya Chen: Understood. Let’s check the wireless adapter power settings and driver version.

09:18:44 Agent notes: Guided customer to Device Manager > Network Adapters > Contoso Wireless AX201 > Properties. Customer reported driver version 23.40.1.5. Advised disabling “Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power.”
09:24:11 Agent notes: Customer also had Windows setting enabled for aggressive battery-saving on wireless adapter under advanced power plan. Changed to Maximum Performance on battery and plugged in.
09:29:52 Agent notes: Ran built-in network troubleshooter. It reset the adapter and reported “Default gateway not available” corrected.
09:34:06 Agent notes: Sent current Contoso-certified wireless package link and guided installation. Customer completed install successfully after one restart.

Customer: It came back online after the restart. Anything else I should test?
Agent Maya Chen: Please put the system to sleep for 2 minutes, wake it, and test browsing.
Customer: Just did that. It reconnected immediately this time.
Agent Maya Chen: Good sign. I also recommend disabling Fast Startup if the issue returns, since network initialization after sleep can be affected.

09:46:33 Final agent note: Customer browsed several sites, streamed a short video, and confirmed no drop for 15 minutes. Provided summary in email with steps completed: driver update, adapter power setting change, power plan adjustment. Case resolved during contact.
Status: Closed - Resolved

2025-03-02 16:03:57 | Ticket ID: CT-557014 | Agent: Daniel Ruiz
Customer opened a web ticket reporting a sticky “E” key on the built-in keyboard of the Contoso AuraBook 14. Description: “The E key sometimes feels gummy and repeats twice. No liquid spill that I know of. Started gradually over the last week.” Customer requested advice before seeking repair because the rest of the keyboard was functioning normally.

16:11:20 Agent note: Replied by email with initial triage questions about environmental debris, use pattern, and whether issue occurs in BIOS/password field versus only in Windows. Customer answered at 16:37 that the repeat occurred in browser, Notes, and sign-in field, so likely hardware or debris rather than one application.

2025-03-03 10:08:49 Follow-up call logged.
Agent Daniel Ruiz: Thanks for answering those questions. Since the behavior happens before apps fully load, let’s try a non-invasive cleaning procedure first.
Customer: That’s fine. I didn’t spill anything, but I do use it in the kitchen sometimes.
Agent Daniel Ruiz: That could explain residue or crumbs under the cap. Please power the unit off completely.

10:12:02 Agent notes: Instructed customer to hold unit at slight angle and use short bursts of compressed air around affected key in a circular pattern. Customer did not have compressed air immediately available. Sent illustrated care article and advised temporary workaround using Filter Keys off and keyboard repeat delay medium-long if double-entry continued.

2025-03-05 14:22:15 Customer replied by portal after trying cleaning. “Compressed air helped a lot. Key no longer sticks, but occasionally feels slightly different from the others.”
14:31:40 Agent note: Offered optional service if issue worsened. Asked customer to test key travel using keyboard diagnostic page and external text editor.
2025-03-06 09:07:28 Customer update: “Typed for about 30 minutes this morning. No repeat and no sticking now.”
09:15:11 Final agent note: Issue likely due to debris under keycap; no further action requested. Advised customer to avoid vacuum attachments that could remove keycap. Case closed as resolved by cleaning guidance.
Status: Closed - Resolved

2025-05-19 11:27:43 | Ticket ID: CT-582406 | Agent: Priya Nair
Customer initiated chat because a Windows update appeared stuck at 87% overnight on the AuraBook 14. Customer message: “I left it updating. This morning it still says Working on updates 87%. I’m afraid to force it off.”

Chat transcript excerpt:
Agent Priya Nair: I’m glad you checked before shutting it down. How long has the same percentage been displayed?
Customer: At least 7 hours.
Agent Priya Nair: That is long enough to investigate. Do you see spinning dots, and is the drive activity light blinking occasionally?
Customer: The dots are moving. Light blinks every now and then.
Agent Priya Nair: That can mean it is still processing, but we can use the safest next step if it does not advance.

11:33:10 Agent notes: Walked customer through waiting an additional 20 minutes while connected to power. No progress beyond 87%.
11:54:26 Agent notes: Advised hard power-off only after confirming prolonged stall and no error code shown. Customer held power button 10 seconds and restarted.
11:58:03 Agent notes: System booted to “Undoing changes made to your computer,” then returned to desktop successfully.
12:05:42 Agent notes: Opened Windows Update settings with customer and reviewed failed cumulative update entry. Disk space available was 18.6 GB, sufficient. Noted third-party VPN driver and paused security tool may have interfered.
12:12:17 Agent notes: Ran Windows Update troubleshooter; it reset update components. Guided customer to open elevated command prompt and execute DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, then sfc /scannow. DISM completed normally. SFC found corrupt files and repaired them.
12:41:55 Agent notes: Asked customer to disconnect nonessential USB devices and temporarily pause the third-party security app real-time scan during retry. Customer retried update.
13:09:09 Customer: It got past 87 and restarted.
13:22:31 Customer: I’m back in. It says up to date now.
Agent Priya Nair: Excellent. Please check your apps and files normally open.
Customer: Looks good. Thank you, I was worried I’d broken it.

13:29:18 Final agent note: Confirmed update success and normal boot. Recommended creating restore point and keeping at least 15 GB free before major updates. Sent recap email. Case resolved.
Status: Closed - Resolved

2025-07-28 18:41:04 | Ticket ID: CT-611973 | Agent: Leo Martinez
Customer contacted support through portal about repeated app sign-in failures with Contoso Notes Cloud on the AuraBook 14. Customer stated the app launched but would return to the sign-in screen after entering correct password. Web sign-in on browser worked. Customer specified issue started after changing account password a few days earlier.

18:49:36 Agent note: Reviewed customer description and suspected stale authentication token in app cache or credential manager conflict rather than account issue, because browser login was successful.

2025-07-29 08:15:22 Live chat started.
Customer: Browser login works, but the desktop Notes app just loops back to sign in.
Agent Leo Martinez: Thanks for confirming. That usually points to a local cached token. We’ll clear that first.
Customer: Okay.
Agent Leo Martinez: Please close the Notes app completely, including the tray icon if present.

08:18:10 Agent notes: Guided customer to Settings > Apps > Contoso Notes Cloud > Advanced options > Terminate, then Repair. Customer tested; issue persisted.
08:24:47 Agent notes: Proceeded with Reset of app data after customer confirmed notes were synced in web view.
08:29:03 Agent notes: Customer signed in again; same looping behavior.
08:34:25 Agent notes: Opened Credential Manager and found two stored generic credentials associated with old Notes Cloud token. Removed stale entries. Also checked system date/time and time zone; both correct.
08:39:56 Agent notes: Advised customer to run wsreset and restart the app installation service. Customer complied.
08:47:12 Customer: I’m in now. My notes are loading.
Agent Leo Martinez: Great. Do you still see repeated prompts?
Customer: No, it signed in normally this time.

08:51:20 Agent notes: Monitored customer through relaunch test. Second launch retained account session correctly.
08:56:04 Final agent note: Root cause likely stale cached credentials after password change. Cleared credential entries and reset app state. Issue resolved. Sent instructions in case customer changes password again in future.
Status: Closed - Resolved

2025-08-09 13:06:51 | Ticket ID: CT-618245 | Agent: Hannah Brooks
Customer submitted a support question asking whether the Contoso USB-C Travel Dock Mini would support dual external monitors with the AuraBook 14, and whether the dock could power the laptop at the same time. Inquiry was pre-sales/use guidance only; no device fault reported.

13:12:33 Agent note: Reviewed AuraBook 14 model capabilities listed in internal compatibility reference. Confirmed USB-C port supports DisplayPort Alt Mode and charging. Dual-monitor support depends on resolution/refresh combination through dock.

13:16:04 Email response sent:
“Your Contoso AuraBook 14 can use the USB-C Travel Dock Mini for external displays and power delivery through a single USB-C connection. Typical supported combinations are two external 1080p displays at standard refresh, or one higher-resolution display depending on bandwidth. If you plan to use two monitors plus several USB peripherals, a powered dock is recommended for best stability. The dock can charge the laptop simultaneously when connected to an adequate power adapter.”

13:17:22 Agent note: Included caution that some monitor/adapter combinations may require certified HDMI/DisplayPort cables. Also mentioned that if customer is using the laptop lid closed, they should configure sleep settings accordingly.

2025-08-10 09:03:58 Customer reply: “That answers it. Mostly two 1080p screens for desk use. Thanks.”
09:11:05 Final agent note: Information request completed; no troubleshooting required.
Status: Closed - Answered

2025-08-21 15:24:39 | Ticket ID: CT-623907 | Agent: Nora Patel
Customer reported that the Contoso AuraBook 14 had become unusually hot during light use and had shut down twice in one week. Customer description from intake form: “Bottom gets very warm even with just browser and email open. Fan sounds loud for a while, then once it turned off suddenly. Happened again yesterday during a video call.” Customer indicated concern but did not report visible damage, liquid exposure, or blocked vents.

15:31:18 Agent note: Reviewed intake details. Customer’s wording suggested possible thermal condition under moderate workload. Because the customer submitted through asynchronous web form and was not available for immediate live troubleshooting, provided a standard knowledge-base article covering overheating prevention and thermal checks.

15:35:40 Email sent by Agent Nora Patel:
“Thank you for contacting Contoso support. If your AuraBook 14 is running hot or shutting down unexpectedly, please review the following steps:
1) Use the device on a hard, flat surface and ensure side/bottom vents are unobstructed.
2) Check for dust buildup around vents.
3) Restart the laptop and install available system and BIOS updates.
4) In Task Manager, close apps using unusually high CPU.
5) Test with the power mode set to Balanced rather than Best performance.
6) See our article KB-THERM-204: ‘Laptop runs hot or powers off unexpectedly.’
If the issue continues after these steps, reply to this message with the results and available times for live troubleshooting.”

15:42:57 Agent internal note: No logs or diagnostics collected in this interaction. No remote session performed. No fan-profile reset performed. Awaiting customer reply.

2025-08-24 10:18:11 Automated follow-up email sent requesting update.
2025-08-29 10:18:37 Automated follow-up email sent requesting update.
2025-09-02 10:19:02 Agent note: No response received from customer after article delivery and follow-up attempts. Closing per no response workflow. If customer returns, resume with live thermal troubleshooting and diagnostics.
Status: Closed - Customer Did Not Respond

Reviewer notes by Sofia Kim, 08:11:39:
Imported diagnostic does not show hardware fan failure. Peak temperature of 96 C under simulation is high but not by itself proof of defect, especially with Best performance mode and heavy background activity. The kernel-power entries align with customer’s earlier narrative of sudden shutdowns, though cause remains unconfirmed. Notable that previous August ticket appears to have ended after KB article only, with no live step completion and no remote corrective actions performed at that time. Current package shows firmware generally current and no storage or memory fault. Recommend, if customer reports recurring heat/shutdown behavior again, obtaining live reproduction details, checking process load immediately before event, and performing interactive thermal mitigation steps rather than article-only guidance.

Additional log excerpts:

Reviewer closing summary, 08:15:22:
Diagnostic package archived. No component failure code generated. Evidence indicates elevated thermal behavior under performance-biased settings and background load, with prior abrupt shutdown records present in OS logs. No resolution action taken in this report entry; findings preserved for case history reference.

2025-10-14 09:12:44 | Ticket ID: CS-541882 | Agent: Maya Chen
Customer contacted Contoso support through chat regarding intermittent Wi-Fi drops on a Contoso AuraBook 14. Customer reported that over the previous three days, the laptop would remain connected to the home network for roughly 10 to 20 minutes and then show “No Internet, secured,” while other devices on the same router stayed online. Customer noted the issue was most noticeable during video meetings and while streaming music. Customer had already restarted the router once and rebooted the laptop twice without permanent improvement.

09:14:03 | Maya Chen
Verified device model as AuraBook 14 and confirmed Windows was loading normally with no other hardware symptoms. Asked customer whether the failure occurred only on the 5 GHz band or also on 2.4 GHz. Customer replied that both SSIDs had shown the problem, though 5 GHz seemed worse. Guided customer to open Settings > Network & Internet > Wi‑Fi > Hardware properties and provide adapter details. Adapter identified as Contoso Wireless AX221.

09:17:26 | Maya Chen
Collected basic environment notes. Customer uses home router supplied by ISP and had not changed any advanced router settings recently. Customer said issue began after returning from travel and using the laptop on another network for a week. In Event Viewer, customer observed several WLAN AutoConfig warnings but did not understand them. Requested that customer run the built-in network troubleshooter first; troubleshooter reset the adapter and temporarily restored connectivity.

09:22:11 | Maya Chen
Guided customer through Device Manager > Network adapters > Contoso Wireless AX221 > Power Management. The “Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power” box was enabled. Advised disabling that setting. Also checked Advanced properties and changed Preferred Band from “No Preference” to “Prefer 5GHz,” then explained customer could test both bands manually if instability continued. Customer mentioned they often close the lid and move between rooms, so roaming behavior could be contributing.

09:28:40 | Maya Chen
Had customer run Command Prompt as admin and execute:
1) netsh winsock reset
2) netsh int ip reset
3) ipconfig /flushdns
4) shutdown /r /t 0
Customer rejoined the network after restart. Signal level reported as strong. Ran a five-minute ping test to the router with no packet loss during session.

09:39:12 | Maya Chen
Checked driver version using Device Manager. Customer was on driver 22.110.1. Suggested updating through Contoso Support Utility rather than generic Windows catalog. Walked customer to launch Contoso Support Utility > Drivers > Wireless. Utility found newer package 23.4.7. Customer installed the update and rebooted.

09:51:27 | Maya Chen
Post-update verification call continued in chat. Customer connected to a video stream and browsed several sites for around ten minutes without disconnection. Maya documented likely cause as stale wireless stack settings combined with power management on the adapter after use on multiple networks. Recommended forgetting older saved networks not currently used, which customer did for two hotel SSIDs.

09:56:03 | Maya Chen
Agent notes: Issue resolved after network stack reset, power-management change, and wireless driver update. Customer advised to monitor for 48 hours and return if drops recur. No hardware service indicated.

Status: Resolved

2025-07-03 16:04:18 | Ticket ID: CS-497614 | Agent: Daniel Osei
Customer opened a web case about a sticky “E” key on the AuraBook 14 keyboard. Customer stated that the key still registered input but did not spring back properly when pressed on the left side, especially while typing quickly. Customer denied any known liquid spill. Device otherwise functioning normally.

16:06:02 | Daniel Osei
Reviewed symptom description and asked customer to inspect keycap area under bright light. Customer reported a small amount of visible lint or debris around the lower hinge of the key. Advised customer not to pry the keycap off. Explained safe cleaning procedure: power off laptop, disconnect charger, hold unit at a slight angle, use short bursts of compressed air around the affected key from multiple directions, and then lightly brush with a soft anti-static keyboard brush.

16:11:44 | Daniel Osei
Customer performed initial cleaning while on chat and noted slightly improved movement but still occasional sticking. Guided customer to open the on-screen keyboard and a text editor to determine whether issue was electrical or mechanical. All keypresses registered correctly; repeated press test showed no missed inputs, only slower mechanical return.

16:15:29 | Daniel Osei
Suggested a second cleaning pass and asked customer to check whether a silicone keyboard cover was installed. Customer confirmed they had been using a thin aftermarket cover for travel. Advised removing cover and testing because edge pressure can sometimes alter key travel on low-profile keys. Customer removed cover and immediately reported more normal feel.

16:20:55 | Daniel Osei
Conducted another typing test with customer dictating several sentences. Customer stated the key no longer stuck and felt noticeably better, though slightly different from neighboring keys. Daniel explained that residual debris can work free gradually and instructed customer to avoid pressing the key sideways and not to introduce cleaning fluids.

16:24:08 | Daniel Osei
Agent notes: Mechanical issue appears caused by debris plus pressure from third-party keyboard cover. Input matrix normal. Customer satisfied with current behavior. Sent follow-up email with keyboard cleaning best practices and instructions to return if sticking worsens or spreads to additional keys.

Status: Resolved

2025-03-21 11:31:57 | Ticket ID: CS-462203 | Agent: Priya Nair
Customer called in after a Windows update appeared to stall overnight on the AuraBook 14. Customer said the laptop had displayed “Working on updates 91%” for more than two hours the previous evening, then after a forced restart it booted to a spinning circle and eventually entered Automatic Repair once before loading Windows. Customer was concerned about possible file loss and slow startup.

11:34:10 | Priya Nair
Confirmed customer could still sign into Windows desktop. Asked whether files and applications were present; customer confirmed documents were intact. System was slower than usual and Settings > Windows Update showed a failed cumulative update with retry pending. Guided customer to collect update history and disk space numbers. Customer had approximately 12 GB free on the system drive.

11:39:46 | Priya Nair
Explained low free space can contribute to update failures. Walked customer through Storage Sense cleanup. Removed temporary files, previous update cleanup items, and emptied recycle bin after customer review. Free space increased to 24 GB. Next, asked customer to disconnect nonessential USB accessories; only a mouse receiver had been attached.

11:45:03 | Priya Nair
Ran Windows Update troubleshooter; troubleshooter reported “Service registration is missing or corrupt” and attempted repair. Then opened admin Command Prompt and executed:
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow
Customer remained on call during scan. SFC found corrupted files and repaired them successfully.

12:03:18 | Priya Nair
Stopped update services and cleared SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 folders using guided commands. Restarted Windows Update and initiated new check. The cumulative update downloaded again. Customer asked whether the earlier forced restart had damaged hardware; explained symptoms indicated software inconsistency rather than a hardware fault.

12:24:32 | Priya Nair
Update installed successfully after reboot. Startup returned to expected speed. Checked Reliability Monitor; prior installation failure logged, followed by successful update. Recommended maintaining at least 20 GB free space for major updates when possible and allowing updates to complete while plugged in.

12:28:01 | Priya Nair
Agent notes: Windows servicing corruption and low disk space likely caused the stalled update. Resolved through cleanup, DISM/SFC, and update component reset. Customer confirmed issue fixed and no missing data.

Status: Resolved

2025-01-09 14:18:05 | Ticket ID: CS-438977 | Agent: Leo Martinez
Customer initiated chat to ask about signing in to the Contoso Notes companion app on the AuraBook 14. Customer said the app had worked previously but now displayed “Unable to verify account. Try again later.” Browser sign-in to the same Contoso account was successful. Customer mainly used the app to sync notes between the laptop and phone.

14:20:27 | Leo Martinez
Verified there was no broader outage reported at the time. Customer had recently changed the account password after receiving a routine security prompt. Asked whether the app had been updated and whether date/time on the laptop were correct. Customer confirmed app had updated automatically last week. Time zone was correct, but the clock was off by about four minutes.

14:24:51 | Leo Martinez
Explained that clock skew can interfere with token validation. Guided customer to set time automatically and sync now from Date & Time settings. Customer did so. Retried sign-in in Contoso Notes; same error persisted. Cleared app cache from Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Contoso Notes > Advanced options > Terminate > Repair > Reset. Customer signed back in but encountered a blank white sign-in window.

14:31:16 | Leo Martinez
Asked customer to verify whether any VPN or filtering software was running. Customer reported a privacy extension in the default browser and a DNS filtering utility. Suggested temporarily disabling the DNS utility and setting network DNS to automatic for testing. After change, the app sign-in page loaded fully. Customer entered credentials and completed sign-in.

14:37:08 | Leo Martinez
Once signed in, prior notes began syncing. Customer confirmed newest note from phone appeared on the laptop after about 20 seconds. Leo advised re-enabling any filtering tools one at a time to identify the exact conflict. Customer later reported in chat that the DNS utility’s HTTPS filtering was the cause; leaving app domains unfiltered corrected the behavior.

14:41:55 | Leo Martinez
Agent notes: Resolved app authentication issue by correcting system time, resetting app state, and removing DNS filtering interference during sign-in. No account-side action required. Sent customer a brief list of excluded domains to preserve app sync.

Status: Resolved

2024-12-02 10:07:33 | Ticket ID: CS-421540 | Agent: Hannah Brooks
Customer reached support with a question about accessory compatibility for the Contoso AuraBook 14. Customer planned to purchase an external monitor and wanted to know whether the laptop’s USB-C port could support display output and charging at the same time through a dock. Customer also asked whether Contoso-branded sleeves were available in the correct size.

10:09:02 | Hannah Brooks
Reviewed AuraBook 14 port capabilities from device specification reference. Confirmed the model’s USB-C port supports data, DisplayPort over USB-C, and power input. Explained that with a compatible dock or USB-C monitor, single-cable video output is supported, though final display resolution and refresh rate depend on the dock, cable quality, and monitor capabilities.

10:12:47 | Hannah Brooks
Customer specifically asked whether dual external displays would be possible. Explained that many docks can provide multiple displays through DisplayPort Alt Mode or DisplayLink-based solutions, but native support varies by dock chipset and monitor configuration. Recommended checking dock documentation for the intended resolution setup and ensuring the dock provides sufficient power delivery for the laptop during load.

10:16:21 | Hannah Brooks
Customer asked if charging through a third-party dock could damage the battery. Advised that compliant USB-C power delivery chargers and docks are generally acceptable when they meet the required output. Recommended using reputable accessories and avoiding unverified low-wattage adapters for sustained performance tasks.

10:19:58 | Hannah Brooks
Regarding sleeves, confirmed Contoso offered a 14-inch protective sleeve that fits the AuraBook 14. Customer wanted a precise fit for commuting. Provided dimensions and noted that a snug sleeve is normal due to the tapered chassis. Customer also asked whether the sleeve had room for the charger; explained it includes a slim accessory pocket suitable for the compact power adapter and a cable.

10:23:36 | Hannah Brooks
Agent notes: Informational inquiry only. Customer received compatibility guidance for USB-C display/charging and accessory sizing. No technical fault present.

Status: Answered

2024-11-06 08:43:11 | Ticket ID: CS-403118 | Agent: Sofia Petrov
Customer contacted support reporting poor battery runtime on the AuraBook 14. Customer said that when the laptop was new, typical evening use lasted “most of the night,” but over the prior month the battery seemed to drop from 100% to around 30% in just over two hours of web browsing, document editing, and music playback. Customer noticed the chassis also felt warmer than expected during light use. No unexpected shutdowns were reported, but the customer was concerned that battery health had deteriorated.

08:46:25 | Sofia Petrov
Verified power settings and immediate usage pattern. Customer generally used balanced power mode, brightness around 75%, Bluetooth on, and several browser tabs plus a chat app open. Guided customer to open Task Manager sorted by CPU and power usage. Found no runaway process at that moment; browser usage was moderate. Requested battery report generation via powercfg /batteryreport.

08:54:09 | Sofia Petrov
Customer shared key values from the battery report. Full charge capacity was significantly below design capacity relative to expected age and usage. Guided customer through a short thermal and charging behavior questionnaire. Customer stated runtime remained poor even after a full overnight charge and after reducing brightness. No swelling or physical deformation observed. Charger was recognized correctly and battery charged to 100%.

09:01:43 | Sofia Petrov
Asked customer to install the latest BIOS and power-management package from Contoso Support Utility in case firmware-level charging tables required update. Customer completed updates and rebooted. Subsequent quick drain observation over roughly 20 minutes still looked steeper than expected for idle/light use. Sofia documented the device-agent error code BAT-047 based on reported health values and observed discharge pattern.

09:12:18 | Sofia Petrov
Explained that BAT-047 indicates battery health decline beyond expected threshold for the collected telemetry and battery report data. Reviewed next steps and advised customer to back up important files before any in-person or mail-in service interaction, even though no data work was expected. Customer asked whether calibration would help; Sofia explained calibration can improve percentage accuracy but would not restore lost capacity if the cells had degraded.

09:20:37 | Sofia Petrov
Created battery evaluation request and scheduled a follow-up after diagnostic review. Customer preferred minimal downtime because the laptop was used daily. Sofia documented serial readings as captured in software and noted no signs of adapter fault.

2024-11-08 13:15:54 | Ticket ID: CS-403118-FU | Agent: Sofia Petrov
Follow-up contact with customer after diagnostic review. Confirmed collected evidence qualified the unit for battery replacement under the Contoso battery health program. Customer approved proceeding with service. Explained process, expected turnaround, and that only the battery assembly would be replaced unless technicians identified another issue during handling.

13:22:06 | Sofia Petrov
Customer asked whether the new battery would require special setup. Advised that after replacement, normal charging and use were fine; optional best practice is a full charge and several regular cycles to let estimates stabilize. Customer also asked whether current heat during light use was likely related. Explained reduced battery health can coincide with less efficient discharge behavior, though software load still influences temperature.

2024-11-15 17:40:12 | Ticket ID: SV-403118-COMP | Agent: Sofia Petrov
Service completion update recorded. Battery replaced on 2024-11-15 under the Contoso battery health program. New battery serial: CB14-9K27-441805. Program replacement completed. Post-service notes indicate charging and discharge checks passed, adapter handshake normal, and no further battery alerts present.

17:44:33 | Sofia Petrov
Customer notified of completed replacement and advised to observe runtime over the next week. Customer later replied by email that initial runtime already seemed much better during evening use.

Status: Resolved

本次诊断触发背景：
客户此前历史中曾记录散热偏高、风扇噪声增大以及在高负载情境下偶发自动关机；历史记录显示曾执行过 REMOTE FAN-PROFILE RESET，状态为 COMPLETED，但后续客户反馈问题仍持续。因此本次采集重点围绕温度、风扇响应、功耗与意外关机事件进行。

温度与风扇数据摘要：
1. 待机至轻载阶段：
系统空闲 8 分钟后，CPU 封装温度维持在中高区间，较同型号常见空闲值偏高；GPU 温度轻微偏高但未达到立即保护阈值。风扇转速在轻载下未完全降至低档，存在持续中速巡航现象。
2. 中负载阶段：
启动浏览器多标签、视频会议测试流与文档同步任务后，CPU 温度攀升速度较快，风扇在约 20 至 40 秒内提升转速，但降温效率一般。表面温度模型估算显示键盘上沿及转轴附近热量聚集更明显。
3. 高负载短测阶段：
在短时处理器压力测试与图形混合负载下，CPU 温度触及热控制上限附近，系统出现明显降频；风扇已拉升到高转速，但温度回落幅度有限。测试为保护设备安全而提前终止，未持续进行长时满载。

事件日志摘要：
1. 系统日志中可见多次 Kernel-Power 非正常关机记录，时间点与客户先前描述的黑屏自动关机时段部分接近。
2. 未见持续性的蓝屏转储记录，说明多次关机更接近保护性掉电或热相关保护触发，而非典型系统崩溃。
3. 近几个月内网络、更新、应用登录相关错误零星存在，但均不构成当前主要异常来源，且与既往已解决问题记录一致。

散热控制相关检查：
1. 风扇控制服务可启动，未发现服务缺失。
2. 风扇曲线配置文件可读取，未出现损坏或缺失标记。
3. 嵌入式控制器返回的风扇反馈转速可读，说明并非“完全无转速上报”的简单通讯故障。
4. 结合历史可知，REMOTE FAN-PROFILE RESET 已执行完成，但本次采集仍观察到轻载温度偏高、高负载温升过快、自动关机日志存在，表明先前重置未能排除根因。

分析工程师说明：
从现有日志和传感器结果看，设备并非单纯的软件显示误报。风扇能响应、系统也会执行热降频，但在较常见的中高负载下温度上升过快，且曾出现与热保护相符的非正常关机记录。由于历史上网络、键盘、Windows 更新、应用登录及配件兼容性等问题均已分别解决，当前异常与这些普通使用问题无直接关联。尤其需要注意的是，约三个月前工单中执行的 REMOTE FAN-PROFILE RESET 虽已完成，但客户随后明确反馈过热持续，和本次诊断结果相互印证。

Customer contacted support through chat regarding intermittent Wi-Fi drops on a Contoso AuraBook Pro 16. Customer: "It reconnects if I disconnect and reconnect, but I have to do that several times a day."
Agent Maya Ortiz: "I can help check whether the adapter is entering a low-power state or whether the driver stack needs to be refreshed."
Customer: "That makes sense because it seems worse after sleep."

Initial intake notes:
- Device confirmed as Contoso AuraBook Pro 16.
- Windows network icon intermittently changing from full bars to globe icon.
- Customer using dual-band home router; SSID visible and strong signal at desk location.
- No VPN active during testing.
- Customer had already restarted the router once with no lasting improvement.

Troubleshooting performed during session:
09:18:42 - Guided customer to forget both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz saved profiles for the home network and reconnect with a fresh profile.
09:24:07 - Checked Device Manager settings for the Contoso Wireless AX adapter. Power management option "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power" was enabled.
09:27:19 - Disabled adapter power-saving shutdown setting.
09:31:55 - Ran Windows network troubleshooter; tool reset the adapter and reported corrected gateway association issue.
09:36:10 - Agent instructed customer to open an elevated command prompt and run ipconfig /flushdns, netsh winsock reset, and netsh int ip reset.
09:43:28 - Customer rebooted device.
09:51:03 - After reboot, customer reconnected to the home Wi-Fi and remained connected for 12 minutes without drop during active browsing.
09:56:44 - Agent checked installed driver version with customer; driver was two revisions behind current validated package for the AuraBook Pro 16.
10:03:11 - Customer downloaded and installed updated Contoso wireless driver package provided by support.
10:15:27 - Post-install reboot completed.
10:22:06 - Customer performed sleep/wake test twice. Connection resumed normally both times, no loss of internet observed.

Agent notes:
The symptom pattern strongly matched a known interaction between an older wireless driver build and aggressive adapter power management after sleep resume. Router replacement was not indicated because issue did not affect other devices and was reproducible around the laptop’s sleep cycle. Customer was patient and able to follow steps closely. Explained that if drops return, we would capture WLAN report logs, but based on current behavior no escalation was necessary.

Resolution:
